Title: Reference-condition MISO versus SISO statistics
Caption: Reference-condition MISO versus SISO statistics. This figure uses the proof250 presentation proof-of-concept simulation (N = 250 independent families) and is not final-paper evidence. Analysis context: recording duration: 300 s; Welch: 128 s, 50% overlap. Points and curves represent arithmetic means across families; the associated source-data files report SD, valid family count, standard error, 95% confidence interval for every available group or cell. The prespecified display threshold is 5 valid families; groups below this threshold are insufficient for inferential interpretation. Black rings mark reported P < 0.05; the MAP complex-error comparison is the prespecified unadjusted primary test, while the remaining five outcomes form one Benjamini-Hochberg family. Model advantage is log10((SISO error + epsilon)/(MISO error + epsilon)) (epsilon = 1e-12); positive values indicate lower MISO error, zero indicates equal error, and negative values indicate lower SISO error.

Analysis context: recording duration: 300 s; Welch: 128 s, 50% overlap. The grouped axis uses exact configured values for ridge lambda. Points and curves represent arithmetic means across families; the associated source-data files report SD, valid family count, total assigned family count, standard error, 95% confidence interval for every available group or cell. The prespecified display threshold is 5 valid families; groups below this threshold are insufficient for inferential interpretation. Black dots or rings mark adjusted P < 0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction across the exact ridge values separately within each pathway model-advantage outcome; raw and adjusted P values are reported in the source data. Model advantage is log10((SISO error + epsilon)/(MISO error + epsilon)) (epsilon = 1e-12); positive values indicate lower MISO error, zero indicates equal error, and negative values indicate lower SISO error.

Title: True PETCO2 delay by applied timing misalignment
Caption: True PETCO2 delay by applied timing misalignment. This figure uses the proof250 presentation proof-of-concept simulation (N = 250 independent families) and is not final-paper evidence. Analysis context: recording duration: 300 s; Welch: 128 s, 50% overlap. The true petco2 response delay (s) axis uses exact configured values. The applied petco2 timing misalignment (s) axis uses exact configured values. Heatmap color represents the arithmetic mean across families; the associated source-data files report SD, valid family count, total assigned family count, standard error, 95% confidence interval for every available group or cell. The prespecified display threshold is 5 valid families; cells below this threshold remain gray and receive no mean color. Black dots or rings mark adjusted P < 0.05 after Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction across all displayed x-by-y cells separately within each pathway model-advantage map; raw and adjusted P values are reported in the source data. Model advantage is log10((SISO error + epsilon)/(MISO error + epsilon)) (epsilon = 1e-12); positive values indicate lower MISO error, zero indicates equal error, and negative values indicate lower SISO error.
